sections.h2: What are the routes to a closing for a Bernards Township house?
sections.html:
A Bernards Township owner can put the house on the market, sell it to a buyer found privately, or accept a cash bid for the property as it stands. The township layers its own pre-sale steps over state rules, so the actual pace depends on how quickly permits and inspections get cleared.

With homes valued around $814,800 at the median, many buyers finance, and a listing draws them. A cash bid answers different problems: an inherited house in Basking Ridge, a property whose permits were never closed, a rental after the tenant leaves, or a seller who needs a date that will hold.

  • Agent listing: the highest potential price, a longer timeline and repair talks after the inspection.
  • Private sale: no agent fee, with pricing, marketing and township paperwork on your desk.
  • Cash buyer: condition does not stall the sale, and the bid is reduced for the work required.

sections.h2: How do the Census numbers describe Bernards Township homeowners?
sections.html:
Housing values here sit far above the national median of $332,700. The Census Bureau puts the township at 28,594 residents in July 2025. Owners live in 83.1 percent of the housing units. Households bring in $194,107 at the median and $109,797 per person, and rent at the median is $2,476.

Adults here are highly educated, with 74.2 percent holding a bachelor's degree or higher. Foreign-born residents are 25.3 percent of the population, and 24.1 percent of people are under 18. A language other than English is spoken at home by 29.4 percent of those age 5 and up. Monthly owner costs reach the top bracket the survey reports: $4,000 or more with a mortgage, $1,500 or more without one.

At these price levels buyers expect a clean permit file, and the township checks for one before any residential sale anyway.

sections.h2: Where is Bernards Township and what is it made of?
sections.html:
Bernards sits at the eastern end of the Somerset Hills and covers 24.33 square miles, nearly all of it land. The Second Watchung Mountain bounds the southwest, the Dead River swamp lies to the south, and the Great Swamp National Wildlife Refuge, the Passaic River and Millington Gorge form the eastern edge. Within the township are Basking Ridge, Liberty Corner, Lyons, Franklin Corners, Mount Horeb, Madisonville and part of The Hills, and the Martinsville ZIP Code 08836 covers a piece of it too.

The area was chartered in 1760 as Bernardston Township and incorporated as Bernards Township on February 21, 1798. Far Hills split off in 1921 and Bernardsville in 1924. Voters turned down a borough of Basking Ridge by better than four to one. The township now has 138.86 miles of roads and neighbors Bedminster, Bernardsville, Bridgewater, Warren, Harding and Long Hill.

sections.h2: What must a Bernards Township seller obtain before closing?
sections.html:
Two things, both issued from 277 South Maple Avenue in Basking Ridge. The first is an inspection and certification of smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and a fire extinguisher from the Bureau of Fire Prevention. The second is a Construction Records Clearance from the Code Enforcement Division. The township's selling guide, revised June 2026, says to create a free account on its online portal to apply.

The clearance rule in the township code says a Construction Records Clearance is required before the sale of any residential structure, and both owner and purchaser can be held responsible if one is not issued. The inspector checks records for open construction or zoning permits, and any open permit must have its final inspection before the clearance issues. File at least 10 business days before the change of ownership. A violation carries a fine up to $1,000, up to 90 days in jail or up to 90 days of community service.

  • Create the free account on the township's online portal and file both applications.
  • Close any open construction or zoning permit before the records inspection.
  • Schedule the fire safety inspection for smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and the extinguisher.
  • Send the clearance fee with the application, using the tier that matches your closing date.

The code exempts several transfers when no one changes occupancy, including title corrections, a transfer between spouses and a transfer by or to an executor or administrator distributing an estate. Mortgage refinancing and home equity loans are exempt as well.

sections.h2: How are Bernards Township property taxes set and paid?
sections.html:
The Tax Collector posts a 2026 total rate of $1.661. Of that, $0.275 funds the county, $0.030 county open space, $1.077 the school district, $0.246 the municipality and $0.033 the library. Four installments fall on the first of February, May, August and November, and the 10th of each of those months is the last day of grace. Postmarks do not count; the payment must be physically in the office.

Collections reached 99.50 percent of the 2025 levy across 10,358 tax accounts and 7,231 sewer accounts counted on January 1, 2026. Sewer bills follow their own cycle, due January 1 and July 1 with a 30-day grace period. A closing in the middle of a quarter is prorated, so get a current balance on both the tax and sewer accounts.

Veteran and senior deductions exist. Seniors qualify at 65 or older on October 1 of the prior year, if they live in the home and stay under the income limit; tell your attorney if a deduction is in place.

sections.h2: Do floods affect a sale in Bernards Township?
sections.html:
They can. The Passaic River runs along the township's edge, and the township keeps a flood information page with flood zone maps for buildings, floodways, open space and township property. It also lists its National Flood Insurance Program Class 7 approval and links to FEMA maps and elevation guides.

Ask a buyer's lender whether the property needs flood insurance, and look up the parcel on the township and FEMA maps before you list. A seller who can show an elevation certificate or a clear zone designation answers a common buyer question in the first week.

sections.h2: What do transit, roads and schools add to Bernards Township listings?
sections.html:
Interstate 78, Interstate 287 and U.S. Route 202 serve the township. NJ Transit's Gladstone Branch stops at Basking Ridge and Lyons stations on the way to Hoboken Terminal, and Lakeland Bus Lines runs a Route 78 rush-hour service from Bedminster to the Port Authority Bus Terminal. Mean travel time to work is 32.5 minutes.

The Bernards Township School District runs six schools, among them Cedar Hill, Liberty Corner, Mount Prospect and Oak Street elementary schools, William Annin Middle School and Ridge High School. Ridge High School won a National Blue Ribbon award in 2009 to 2010. The district reported 4,874 students in 2020 to 2021. Private options include Pingry School's upper campus in Basking Ridge and Saint James School.

sections.h2: What changes when a Bernards Township buyer pays cash?
sections.html:
Paying cash takes out the lender's appraisal and most repair haggling. The Construction Records Clearance, the Bureau of Fire Prevention certification and the state transfer fee all stay in place. Agree up front who files each application, because the clearance fee climbs as closing nears.

Weigh offers by what you keep. A listing may fetch more, but commission, staging, inspection credits and holding costs come out of it. Above $1,000,000 the buyer owes an extra 1 percent fee beyond the seller's own transfer fee.

faqs.q: Is a smoke detector certificate the only thing Bernards Township asks for?
faqs.a: No. The Code Enforcement Division also issues a Construction Records Clearance before a residential sale. Its review looks for open construction or zoning permits, which need final inspections before the clearance is released.

faqs.q: How much does a Construction Records Clearance cost in Bernards Township?
faqs.a: $40 if it reaches the township more than 10 calendar days ahead of closing, $75 inside 10 days and $125 inside 4 days. The township asks for the application at least 10 business days before ownership changes.

faqs.q: When are Bernards Township property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first of February, May, August and November, with grace through the 10th. The money must be in the Tax Collector's hands by then, since a postmark proves nothing. Sewer bills are due January 1 and July 1.

faqs.q: Which transfers skip the Bernards clearance?
faqs.a: A transfer is exempt when occupancy stays the same. The code lists a deed correction, a transfer between spouses, an estate distribution by an executor or administrator, and refinancing or home equity loans.

faqs.q: Does the buyer ever pay a transfer fee in New Jersey?
faqs.a: Only when the price is above $1,000,000. The seller pays the standard realty transfer fee in every sale, and the buyer owes an added 1 percent when consideration exceeds that line.
